findings.F1: Within each coin, the 14 days after the bars where the 10-day volatility stood lowest against the 60-day volatility (bottom fifth, log ratio -0.73) ended -7.2 % below the coin's mean 14-day return (t -3.25 over 41 days, 154 cases). The other fifths ranged from +0.6 % to +3.4 %. The slope on the ratio's rank was +0.53 (day-clustered t 2.26, 732 cases, 79 days) and positive in 16 of 16 coins. It held with the 30-day volatility level in the regression (t 2.32). It is a recent-years effect (2022–2025: t 3.04; 2018–2021: t 0.03). It is horizon-specific: t 0.98 at 7 days, -0.29 at 21 days, 1.10 at 30 days. With the many angles looked at, it is suggestive rather than settled.
findings.F2: A coin's 30-day volatility against its own average leaned against the next move. The 14-day slope on its rank was -0.43 (t -2.09, 131 days) and negative in 16 of 17 coins. Over 30 days, the calmest within-coin third rose +11.5 % against +1.0 % and -0.8 % for the other two thirds (excess +0.23 usual move, t 1.39, 39 days; rank correlation -0.16 over 676 cases). The day-clustered 30-day slope is only t -1.53.
findings.F3: At 30 days the bars show continuation, not reversal. Price near its 60-day high predicted a higher 30-day excess return (slope +0.40, t 1.95, positive in 14 of 15 coins). The top fifth of the 30-day move, scaled to the coin's usual, was followed by +5.1 % excess (t 1.33). The bottom fifth was followed by -6.2 % (t -1.31), with 13 of 15 coins leaning the same way. This is against the brief's overreaction story, though no single cut reaches t 2.
findings.F4: The tested book's gain is not graded by its forecast. Net trade P/L by entry-forecast quartile was +4.9 %, +8.7 %, +4.9 % and +6.3 %, with the top quartile saturated at 20. The tested idea's unusual move is +3.84 % per case with t 1.10 over 99 days. Its trades lost in 2019 (-2.7 %, 45 trades) and 2022 (-1.2 %, 83 trades) and won in 2023–2024 (+13.6 %, +12.3 %). XRP's 35 trades averaged +30.8 %, against -5.4 % for BTC.
findings.F5: The weekday pattern is not real. Once days are taken together across coins, no weekday stands out: the largest |t| is 2.10 (Saturday) among 7 weekdays, and Saturday's mean falls from +0.106 to +0.029 standard deviations between the early and late halves.

ideas.idea: The further a coin's volatility over the past 10 days has fallen below its volatility over the past 60 days, the more its price falls below its usual drift over the next 14 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader refuses longs in a coin whose daily swings have gone unusually quiet against the past two months, and expects the deepest quiet to precede the weakest two weeks.
ideas.name: volatility compression precedes weakness

ideas.idea: The lower a coin's volatility over the past 30 days stands against its own usual volatility, the more its price rises above its usual drift over the next 30 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader favours a coin in its calmest stretches over the same coin in its most turbulent ones for a one-month long.
ideas.name: calm coins outperform next month

ideas.idea: The closer a coin's price stands to its highest close of the past 60 days, the more it rises above its usual drift over the next 30 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader holds a coin trading near its two-month high rather than fading it, and expects the coins furthest below their high to keep lagging.
ideas.name: near-high continuation over month
